text.p: Following are some of the major events to have occurred on October 10 in history.
1813 - Giuseppe Verdi, one of the greatest Italian opera composers, born. Works included "Aida", "Otello" and "Rigoletto".
1825 - Paul Kruger, South African farmer, soldier and statesman, born. President of the South African Republic 1883-1902, he made his mark as the builder of the Afrikaner nation.
1830 - Queen Isabella II of Spain born. Queen from the age of three, her reign was marked by political instability and the rule of military politicians.
1845 - The U.S. Naval School, later the Naval Academy, opened at Annapolis, Maryland.
1874 - The ruling chiefs of Fiji ceded the South Pacific islands to Britain.
1911 - Chinese nationalist leader Sun Yat Sen proclaimed a Republic at Wuchang and began the revolution which overthrew the Manchu dynasty.
1918 - Yigal Allon, Israeli soldier and politician, born. He was one of Israel's top commanders in the 1948 War of Independence and a leading cabinet minister.
1930 - Three U.S. airlines merged to form Transcontinental and Western Airlines (TWA), later TransWorld Airlines.
1965 - The "Vinland Map" was introduced by Yale University as being the first known map of America, drawn about 1440 by Norse explorer Lief Eriksson.
1970 - Fiji, a British colony since 1874, became an independent member of the Commonwealth.
1970 - Quebec Labour Minister Pierre Laporte was kidnapped by Quebec separatists. His body was found on the 17th.

1970 - Edouard Daladier, French politician and three times prime minister during the 1930s, died. As premier he was among the signers of the Munich Pact of 1938, which enabled Nazi Germany to take possession of the Sudetenland.
1973 - U.S. Vice-President Spiro Agnew resigned after being charged with tax evasion.
1975 - Richard Burton and Elizabeth Taylor married for the second time at a remote location in Botswana. They divorced the following year.
1980 - 2,590 people were killed in an earthquake In Algeria which registered up to 7.3 on the Richter scale. The earthquake centred on the town of El Asnam and left 330,000 people homeless.
1982 - The United States imposed sanctions against Poland after the Polish government banned the Solidarity trade union.
1983 - Sir Ralph Richardson, renowned British stage actor, died in London aged 80.
1983 - Israel's Knesset (parliament) confirmed Yitzhak Shamir's appointment as prime minister.
1985 - Yul Brynner, U.S. film and stage actor, died. He starred in many films, but was probably best known for his role in the musical "The King and I", which he played both on screen and on stage.
1985 - Orson Welles, U.S. stage, radio, film and television actor, director and producer, died. His film "Citizen Kane" is regarded as one of the great classics of the cinema.

1995 - Israel began its West Bank pullback and freed hundreds of Palestinian prisoners under a deal with the Palestine Liberation Organisation; some inmates refused to go in solidarity with others left behind.

1995 - A one-day strike by five million public sector workers in France brought railways, buses, underground trains, schools, post offices and a host of other services and state-owned firms to a near-standstill.
1995 - Comoros President Said Mohamed Djohar said it was France's duty to reinstate and protect him after French troops overthrew a mercenary-led coup in the Indian Ocean islands.
